description:
Found during the bedrock-n5h audit; pre-existing.

`add_pid_to_waiting_for_healthy/2` (foreman/impl.ex) only ever prepends. The sole removal is the wholesale clear inside `notify_waiting_for_healthy/1` when health reaches `:ok`. There is no monitor on the waiting caller — `grep -rn 'monitor|:DOWN' lib/bedrock/service/foreman/` returns nothing.

## Failure scenario

`Foreman.wait_for_healthy/2` accepts a finite timeout (foreman.ex:52-54). A caller passes one, the foreman does not reach `:ok` in time, and `GenServer.call` flushes and raises in the caller. Its `from` stays in `waiting_for_healthy` forever.

Two consequences:

- If health later reaches `:ok`, `GenServer.reply/2` sends `{stale_ref, :ok}` into a live process's mailbox where nothing matches it. Harmless in isolation, but it is an unmatched message that accumulates.
- If `:ok` never arrives, the list grows without bound — one entry per timed-out or dead caller, retained for the life of the foreman.

A caller that simply dies while parked has the same effect.

## Why now

bedrock-n5h routes every health change through `settle_health/1`, which means the reply now fires from four call sites rather than one. The leak is unchanged, but the stale-reply path is exercised more often.

## Fix

Monitor the caller when parking it, and drop its entry on `:DOWN`. That also bounds the list naturally. Alternatively record a deadline alongside each `from` and prune expired entries when settling — cheaper, but it duplicates the caller's own timeout and can still retain an entry for a caller that died early.

## Test (write first, must fail)

Park a caller with a short timeout, let it expire, drive health to `:ok`, and assert the list is empty and no message was sent. Separately: park a caller, kill it, assert its entry is dropped.
title: [BUG] waiting_for_healthy is never pruned: a timed-out caller leaks and gets a stale reply
